title: Tree Trunks' Recipe
synopsis: Tree Trunks loses her apple pie recipe card and refuses to believe she has it memorized.
plot:
Tree Trunks' handwritten recipe card, the one she has used for every apple pie she has ever made, blows out the window. She is inconsolable and convinced she can never bake again. Mr. Pig gently points out that she has made ten thousand pies. She says that is not the point.

Finn and Jake chase the card across the Grass Lands. It gets stuck to a bird, then to Cinnamon Bun, then to a kite. Meanwhile, Tree Trunks tries to bake from memory and gets as far as 'apples' before she freezes. Sweet Pig-Trunks knocks the flour off the counter, and Tree Trunks, annoyed, cleans it up, then absentmindedly starts cutting apples, then rolling dough, and has a whole pie in the oven before she notices.

Finn and Jake return with the card, muddy and torn. Tree Trunks reads it and laughs: it doesn't have the recipe on it at all. It has a grocery list from thirty years ago. The recipe was never written down. Mr. Pig frames the grocery list. Everyone eats pie.
transcriptText:
Tree Trunks: Oh no. Oh no no no. The card!
Mr. Pig: What card, dear?
Tree Trunks: My recipe card! It blew right out the window! I'll never bake again!
Mr. Pig: Tree Trunks, you've baked ten thousand pies.
Tree Trunks: And every one of them with that card, Mr. Pig!
Finn: We'll get it back. Jake, go go go!
[The card sticks to a bird.]
Jake: [stretching] Bird! Give me the card, bird!
Bird: Chirp.
[The card sticks to Cinnamon Bun.]
Cinnamon Bun: Why is there a card on me. Why is there always something on me.
[Tree Trunks' kitchen. She stares at an apple.]
Tree Trunks: Apples. Apples, and then... and then...
Sweet Pig-Trunks: [knocks the flour off the counter]
Tree Trunks: Oh, sugar. Look at this mess.
[She sweeps up the flour. She cuts an apple without looking. She rolls out dough while sighing.]
Mr. Pig: Tree Trunks.
Tree Trunks: What?
Mr. Pig: Look at the oven.
Tree Trunks: ...When did I do that?
[Finn and Jake burst in, muddy, holding a torn card.]
Finn: We got it! It went through a kite and a pond but we got it!
Tree Trunks: Oh, boys. Oh, bless you. Let me see.
[She reads. A long pause. Then she laughs.]
Jake: What? What's it say?
Tree Trunks: 'Eggs. Butter. Sugar. Ask Mr. Pig about the fence.' It's a grocery list. From... oh, thirty years ago.
Finn: The recipe's not on it?
Tree Trunks: It was never on it, sweetheart. I just liked having it there.
Mr. Pig: I'll frame it.
Tree Trunks: Pie's ready. Everyone sit down.
